attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words, in his own post, stated in the first person.

semantics.note: 'I believe ... will' and 'anticipate' are firm expectations, not hedges. The Facebook part is unconditional. The Instagram part keeps its antecedent ('as things get difficult'). No deadline was given.

contract.note: The plain reading (sustained audience contraction, then closure or lasting marginality) is ordinary and fair. The contract correctly says continued operation at a finite date cannot contradict an open-ended forecast.

evidence.note: Meta Q3 2025 remarks report growing daily actives. This is a company disclosure at a finite date and cannot settle an eventual-death forecast.
Instagram says it has 3B MAU (company disclosure). The Instagram antecedent is not established, so this does not settle that clause.
Pew 2025 survey: 71% of US adults use Facebook, stable. US-only self-reports at a finite date; not terminal evidence.
Shows Facebook product activity continuing in 2026. Not an audience measure.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has no conclusive event (no Facebook shutdown). Continued growth up to 2025–26 does not contradict an eventual outcome. The Instagram clause's antecedent is not established. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. The figure is based on press reports, but he asserts it himself.

semantics.note: Firm parts: over $40B on the metaverse, and further billions on GPUs. 'Seems to be intent' is a hedged judgment and is not scored. 'Nobody asked for' is rhetoric.

contract.note: Keeping losses separate from expenditure is strict but defensible. Note that Reality Labs operating losses are a lower bound on its gross expenses. The GPU part needs isolated gen-AI hardware spending, which the speaker did not quantify.

evidence.note: Fortune: Reality Labs lost about $46.5B from 2019 to Q3 2023. Gross expenses must exceed this, which leans toward the metaverse figure, but Reality Labs is not exactly the same scope as 'metaverse'.
Q1 2024 capex of $6.7B, company-wide servers and data centers. Not isolated to gen-AI GPUs.
Meta announced GPU clusters and a 350k H100 target. Shows deployment, but discloses no dollar cost.

reviews.rationale: The metaverse figure leans supported: Reality Labs losses of $46.5B imply larger gross spending, though the segment-to-metaverse mapping is inexact. Nothing in the packet isolates realized gen-AI hardware spending, so the 'further billions' part is not established. The contract needs both parts, so the result is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own causal assertion, in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense causal claim: engagement-maximizing without curation is slowly killing Facebook. Faithful, and the revision correctly removed the added AI-image wording.

contract.note: Reading 'killing' as sustained audience or retention deterioration is ordinary. The period comes from the surrounding data discussion, which is reasonable. Requiring causal evidence is fair.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study of spam and scam AI-image Pages amplified by the Feed. It documents the mechanism, not audience decline or what caused it.
Meta 10-K: worldwide Facebook MAU up 3% and DAU up 6% in 2023. This weighs against a worldwide decline, but by the contract one measure alone cannot contradict, and causation is not addressed.

reviews.rationale: No evidence shows sustained Facebook deterioration caused by the stated incentives. Worldwide MAU and DAU growth weighs against the claim but does not meet the contradiction condition, which requires causal evidence. US and web-only declines are not reproduced here. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own description of Meta AI, in his own post.

semantics.note: The core assertions are preserved. The proposition leaves out 'free' and the question and image capabilities, but the contract restores them. 'Most confusing' is opinion and is not scored.

contract.note: Reading 'property' as the four main apps, 'impossible to disable' as having no complete off setting, and limiting scope to supported-country rollout is an ordinary, fair reading.

evidence.note: Meta's launch post: Meta AI is in search across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, answers questions, and has an 'imagine' image feature. Company disclosure; rollout limited by geography.
May 9, 2024 test: no app setting disables Meta AI on any of the apps. The workarounds are blocking the profile or downgrading the app.
Meta told Global News the general presence cannot be disabled. Group admins can turn off group replies, but the contract treats that as distinct.

reviews.rationale: Contemporary evidence shows Meta AI in all four main apps with question and image features, and no complete user off switch, which Meta itself confirmed. The group-admin control and the workarounds are excluded by the contract. Supported for the April–May 2024 rollout in supported countries.
